newsitem.title: USA: Prescription allergy spray now available over the counter.
newsitem.headline: Prescription allergy spray now available over the counter.

text.p: Sneezing, sniffling, coughing -- Ah, yes, the poetry of allergy season.

McNeil Consumer Products Co., a maker of over-the-counter health products, has started nationwide distribution of a nasal spray for allergy sufferers that until now has only been available by prescription.

Nasalcrom is for relief and prevention of hayfever and other nasal allergies. It contains cromolyn sodium, which acts to prevent mast cells in the nose from releasing histamine and other inflammatory agents, which lead to sneezing, runny nose and other allergy symptoms.
An inhaled version of cromolyn sodium is used in prescription treatments for asthma.

Unlike decongestant sprays, which can raise cardiovascular risk and produce so-called rebound congestion with overuse, and antihistamines, which can cause drowsiness and do not relieve nasal congestion, Nasalcrom is not associated with sedation, agitation or dry mouth.
Nasalcrom also, according to FDA literature, is safe with other medications one may be taking, such as drugs for heart problems or depression.
Nasalcrom, first available by prescription in 1983, recently received Food and Drug Administration approval for over-the-counter sale. Its formulation has remained the same, McNeil said.

A McNeil spokeswoman said that the road from prescription to over-the-counter status was smooth because Nasalcrom "has an excellent safety profile. You can't get addicted and the abuse potential is very small."

She was referring to other over-the-counter nasal sprays, used to unclog the nose, that can only be used for up to three days. Overuse can cause a "rebound" effect, in which the original problem is exacerbated by overuse of a drug.
Nasalcrom is available in drug stores in 100-spray and 200-spray bottles. It costs about $11.99 for the small size and $19.99 for the large size.
For more information, call McNeil at 1-800-962-5357.
A new family of wrist rest products has been introduced by Costa Mesa, Calif.-based Envirogen International Inc., designed to help protect hands and wrists from the effects of prolonged computer use.
The SoftSpot Proline Keyboard and Mousepad wrist supports are soft moulded pads tht cushion the wrists and distribute weight to prevent fatigue.
Using a patented material called Therasoft, the pads help eliminate pressure points, are non-abrasive, antistatic and washable, the company said.

One version, the SoftSpot Keyboard Wrist Support, is designed for use with a regular-style keyboard. The SoftSpot Contour Wrist Support is designed for use with the Microsoft Natural Style Keyboard and similar products.
Both wrist rests come in several colours and cost about $24.95.
For more information, call Envirogen at 1-800-228-8839.
Murray Inc., maker of outdoor equipment, has developed a new line of 20-inch rear bagger lawn mowers that convert between mulching, side discharging and bagging without tools or extra parts.
Murray said it has found that there is increasing demand for smaller, manoeuvrable mowers.
The mowers range in price from about $179 to $317.
For more information call Murray at 1-800-251-8007.
Umix Inc. of Colorado Springs, Colo., has created the Shake It Up formula feeding system.
The dual-chamber bottle is designed to store and feed powdered formula to infants, eliminating problems such as spoilage that can occur when formula is mixed too far in advance of feeding time.
Shake It Up can hold up to eight ounces of fluid. It has a funnel-shaped powder chamber. The fluid and powder are mixed by sliding the top of the bottle and shaking.
By mixing powdered formula only when needed, the occurrance of bacterial growth is reduced, the company said.
Shake It Up bottles are available for $4.99 to $6.99. For more information call 1-888-864-UMIX (8649).
